2 · Control demo · Secs. IV and VI

Tip regulation in the null space of an EE constraint

The controller treats the EE constraint as the primary task and regulates the tip with the null-space motion that the constraint permits. When barriers are defined, a quadratic program replaces the nominal command so that the barrier conditions hold. The workspace runs the simulations of Sec. VI with the plant, the identified model, the controller, and the measurement noise of the paper's simulator.

EE constraints (Sec. IV-A)

ConstraintError \ec(\q)r_c
Free EEnone0
Position-constrained EEp_B^\star-p_B3
Laparoscopic fulcrum(I-uu^{\T})(c-p_B)2

The fulcrum requires the tool axis u, the z axis of \{B\}, to pass through the point c, so the arm can pivot about c, roll about the tool axis, and insert the tool. With J_c=-\partial\ec/\partial\q,

\dot{\bm e}_c=-J_c(\q)\qd,

and the orthogonal projector onto the null space of J_c, whose range has dimension n-r_c, is

N_c=I-J_c^+J_c.

A restoring velocity corrects small deviations from the constraint, and the nominal command adds the null-space motion that regulates the tip:

\qdc=J_c^+k_c\ec,\qquad \qnom=\qdc+N_c\nuv

Tip task in the null space (Sec. IV-B)

\e=p_D^\star-p_D,\qquad v^\star=k_t\e
A:=J_tN_c

The constrained tip Jacobian A is the tip Jacobian restricted to the joint motions that the EE constraint permits. The restoring velocity also moves the tip, so the null-space term tracks the residual reference \vres:=v^\star-J_t\qdc with a damped least-squares inverse:

\nuv=A^{\T}(AA^{\T}+\xi^2I)^{-1}W\vres

Only the component of \vres in \range A can be produced by null-space motion.

Safety and model-validity constraints (Sec. IV-C)

Obstacles, the aperture, cone, and insertion range of the fulcrum, and the identified span domain are written as barrier functions with h(\q)\ge\varepsilon_h. When barriers are defined, the command is the solution of the weighted QP

\begin{aligned}\min_{\qd}\ &\|J_t\qd-v^\star\|^2+w_c\|J_c\qd-k_c\ec\|^2+\mu^2\|\qd\|^2\\ \text{s.t.}\ &\nabla h(\q)^{\T}\qd\ge-\alpha_h\big(h(\q)-\varepsilon_h\big)\ \ \text{for all } h\in\mathcal H,\\ &\qd^-\le\qd\le\qd^+.\end{aligned}
BarrierFunction h
Obstacle clearance\hobs=\min_j\dist(p_j,\mathcal O)-r
Aperture crossing\hap=(\rap-r)\cos\theta-d_c
Tool-axis tilt\hcone=\bar\theta-\theta
Insertion depth\hins=\min(\delta-\delta_{\min},\,\delta_{\max}-\delta)
Span domain \Lspan\hspan=\min_i\min(\lo_i-\ell^-_i,\,\ell^+_i-\lo_i)

Each minimum is imposed as separate inequalities. In the simulations, the clearance is computed to the polyline through the five body points predicted by the identified model, minus a constant margin, and the QP is solved at every control step.

Scenarios (Sec. VI-B)

EE constraintObstaclesTargets
S1position-constrained49
S2laparoscopic fulcrum15
S3laparoscopic fulcrum46, of which T3 and T5 are infeasible by design

Try this

  1. Press Run with S2. The arm pivots about the fulcrum c while the tip visits the five inspection points below the aperture; the tool axis stays within about 0.04 mm of c, and near the targets the span-domain barrier becomes active.
  2. Run S1. With the EE position held, the tip reaches the nine targets around two spheres and two boxes through the reorientation of the EE and the bending of the soft extension.
  3. Run S3. T3 lies inside a sphere and T5 beyond the insertion limit, so the error settles about 50 mm from them while the obstacle or insertion barrier is active, and the run then moves on to the next target.
  4. In S2, turn off the obstacle barrier and restart: the tip reaches the targets more closely, and the soft extension enters the polyp.
  5. Change the EE constraint to a free EE, or to a fulcrum at a finite aperture imposed by barriers only, as on the real setup. With all barriers off, the nominal control law (15), (18) runs without the QP, and the spectral filter can be changed.
  6. Add a target with the sliders: a target that requires spans outside \Lspan settles at the boundary of the identified span domain.

The EE constraint holds to a fraction of a millimeter while the null-space motion actuates the tendons. Near obstacles, at the limits of the fulcrum, and at the boundary of the identified span domain, the barrier conditions of the QP determine how far the tip error can decrease.

Simulation setup (Table IV)

The plant is the UR10 with a 320 mm Cosserat rod and two tendons, integrated at 100 Hz; it solves the quasi-static equilibrium of the rod at the joint angles. The controller receives the joint angles, and the tip and five body points at 20 Hz with Gaussian noise of 0.5 mm standard deviation. It runs at 50 Hz with k_t=1.4\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}, k_c=3.0\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}, \xi=\mu=0.04\,\mathrm{m}, w_c=200, and joint rates up to 17°/s. \Jlq and \Jtr are exact, and \Jspanh is the map identified by the paper's simulator on an 11 × 11 grid of spans (±10 mm), refined online. A target is reached when the tip stays within 4 mm for 8 s, and the run moves on when the error does not decrease for 10 s.

The code is a port of the Python package softext/, and tests/test_web_parity.py checks that both give the same logs. The paper's runs came from its ROS 2 simulator, with another noise realization and message timing, so the numbers here are close to those of Sec. VI but not equal.
